---
title: "The Stream of Ideas"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** When to Start Fresh. **Objective:** triage each new thought during a task into the right place (do now, park, quick question, helper, branch, or later session), and know what undo can and cannot restore. **Time:** about 15 minutes.
<span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): research/session-management.md sources on 2026-11-16 (Claude Code commands, sessions, worktrees, checkpointing and best-practices docs). Claude Code specific unless stated. Parking-lot files are general practice.</span>
Topics in this zone were inspired by Matt Pocock's course LLM Fundamentals (aihero.dev/llm-fundamentals). The explanations here are our own.
:::

Real work does not arrive in a straight line. You start fixing a samplesheet parser and think: "should I switch the aligner? What if I tried a stricter QC threshold? I also want to explore that other idea." If you type every one of those into the same conversation, the **context** (everything the model can see when it writes its next reply, see The Context Window) fills with side tracks. The docs say accuracy and recall degrade as context grows, and the whole conversation is re-sent on every request, so a cluttered session tends to cost more per step. This is how a session ends up with three unrelated tasks that it "re-reads on every turn of the fourth", in the docs' words.

The fix is not to stop having ideas. It is to **triage** each one.

## Terms used here

- **Session:** one saved conversation with the tool, tied to a project folder.
- **Subagent:** a helper the main agent starts. It works in its own separate context and sends back only a summary, so its reading does not pile up in your conversation.
- **Branch (fork):** a copy of the conversation from this point, so you can try something in the copy while the original stays as it was.
- **Git worktree:** a second checkout of the same repository in another folder, so two sessions can edit files without overwriting each other.
- **Checkpoint:** a snapshot Claude Code takes at each prompt you send, so you can roll back with `/rewind`.

## The triage

For each new thought, ask in this order:

1. **Does it block the current task?** Do it now, in this session.
2. **Can it wait?** Park it: write one line in a file and carry on (general practice, see below).
3. **Is it a quick question you do not need on record?** Use `/btw <question>`. It sees the conversation so far, has no tool access (it cannot read files or run commands) and adds nothing to the history.
4. **Is it exploration where you only need a summary?** Ask for a subagent (the built-in Explore helper is a fast read-only searcher), or use `/subtask <task>`, which starts a background helper that inherits the conversation and returns its result here.
5. **Is it a competing approach you want to try for real?** Use `/branch [name]` to copy the conversation (the original stays reachable via `/resume`), or start a second session in its own worktree with `claude --worktree <name>`.
6. **Is it a different task entirely?** Finish the current one, commit a checkpoint of your work, then `/clear` or start a new named session (`claude -n <name>`, or `/rename <name>` inside one).

| New thought | Where it goes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "The parser crashes on this sample ID" (it is the task) | Do now | It blocks you |
| "Maybe we should switch aligner" | Parking-lot line | Cannot change the current fix; no cost to the context |
| "What does this flag do again?" | `/btw` | One answer, no tools, not kept in the history |
| "Where is the aligner configured across the repo?" | Explore subagent or `/subtask` | Heavy reading stays out of your main context; you get a summary |
| "Try the other aligner and compare" | `/branch` or `claude --worktree <name>` | A real attempt that can fail without spoiling the main path |
| "Redo the plots for the other project" | Commit, then `/clear` or a new named session | Different task, different files, different context |

## What is and is not shared

A worktree session isolates file edits only. Per the docs, `claude --worktree <name>` creates `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` on a branch called `worktree-<name>`. Worktrees share the repository's `.git`, and auto memory is per repository, so all worktrees share it. A fresh checkout does not contain gitignored files such as `.env` unless you list them in `.worktreeinclude`, and large data folders need `worktree.symlinkDirectories` or a setup step. Plan for that before you start a pipeline test in one.

`/branch` copies the conversation. Any background helpers still running keep reporting into the branch, not the original.

## Checkpoints and `/rewind`

Every prompt you send is a checkpoint. `/rewind` (aliases `/checkpoint`, `/undo`; or press `Esc` twice on an empty prompt) lets you restore code and conversation, only the conversation, or only the code. The limits matter to bioinformatics: files changed **only through Bash** are not tracked, subagent edits are mostly not restored, and edits outside the session are not tracked. The docs say checkpoints are "not a replacement for version control". A `sed -i` or a script that rewrites a results table is a Bash change (our inference from the limits), so exploring is safe only if you committed first.

## A parking-lot file

**General practice (our inference, not a documented feature):** no official page describes a parking-lot file. Keep it outside what the agent reads every session; the research cautions that a file imported into your instructions costs context each time. Keep it in the repository if the team should see it, in a gitignored file if it is personal, or use an issue tracker for anything that outlives the week.

```markdown
# IDEAS.md  (one line each: date | idea | why it matters | revisit when)
2026-11-16 | Switch aligner to X | Might cut runtime on long reads | after parser fix is merged
2026-11-16 | Stricter QC threshold (Q30 not Q20) | Fewer false variants in low-depth samples | when the test cohort is ready
2026-11-16 | Per-sample coverage plot | Spot dropouts faster | before the next batch
```

## Worked example

You are fixing a samplesheet parser that rejects sample IDs containing a dot.

- "Does the pipeline require the dot at all?" That blocks the fix: **do it now**.
- "Should we switch the aligner?" It cannot change today's fix: **park** it as a line in IDEAS.md.
- "What did `--min-qual` default to again?" A quick fact: **`/btw`**.
- "Where else do we split sample IDs on dots?" Wide reading, only the list matters: **Explore subagent**.
- "Would a stricter QC threshold change the results?" A real experiment: commit the fix, then **`/branch`** or a **worktree** session.
- "I should also tidy the figures for the other project." **Later session**: commit, `/clear`, or `claude -n figures`.

The main session ended with the parser fixed and a short, readable history.

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

Commands the docs confirm: `/btw`, `/subtask`, `/branch`, `/fork`, `/rewind`, `/clear`, `/rename`, `/resume`, `claude -n <name>`, `claude --worktree <name>` (or `-w`). Plan mode (`/plan`, or `Shift+Tab` until the bar shows it) makes Claude read and propose without editing until you approve, which suits a side idea you only want to think through.

## OpenCode + Ollama

Not checked: OpenCode's side-question, branch and worktree features; the research could not find its share and fork pages. Documented on its terminal page: `/new` (alias `/clear`) for a fresh session, `/sessions` to return to one, `/compact`, and `/undo` and `/redo` (these need a git repository). General practice: a parking-lot file and a commit before exploring work in any tool, local models included.
